datasets.title: Central African Republic - Spatial Distribution of Population (2015-2030)
datasets.description: Estimates, total number of people per grid-cell. The dataset is available to download in Geotiff format at a resolution of 3 arc (approximately 100m at the equator). The projection is Geographic Coordinate System, WGS84. The units are number of people per pixel. The mapping approach is Random Forest-based dasymetric redistribution. More information can be found in the Release Statement Please note that these data represent 2025 Alpha release versions, constructed in September 2025. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/worldpop-population-counts-2015-2030-caf]
datasets.details: Disclaimer:The dataset currently represents an alpha version (R2025A) product and may change over the coming year as improvements are made. Data for earlier dates is available directly from WorldPop Bondarenko M., Priyatikanto R., Tejedor-Garavito N., Zhang W., McKeen T., Cunningham A., Woods T., Hilton J., Cihan D., Nosatiuk B., Brinkhoff T., Tatem A., Sorichetta A.. 2025 Constrained estimates of 2015-2030 total number of people per grid square at a resolution of 3 arc (approximately 100m at the equator) R2025A version v1. Global Demographic Data Project - Funded by The Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (INV-045237). WorldPop - School of Geography and Environmental Science, University of Southampton. DOI:10.5258/SOTON/WP00839

lineage.description: Population estimates derived from census data and ancillary geospatial variables using Random Forest-based dasymetric redistribution methodology. Data processed into gridded rasters at 100m and 1km resolution in WGS84 projection for multiple years (2015-2030) to provide baseline population exposure for disaster risk assessment.

sources.name: WorldPop
sources.description: Dasymetric population redistribution model using Random Forest methodology to estimate spatial distribution of population from census and ancillary data sources
